formats.encoding: ASCII, CR LF line ends, one 0x1A end-of-file byte. No binary records, no MBF floats, no 16-bit integers: every number is decimal text (speeds may be fractional).

coordinate_system.map: 25000 x 20000 units = 5 columns x 4 rows of 5000-unit quadrants.
coordinate_system.quadrant_number: 1 + floor(x/5000) + 5*floor(y/5000) (row-major). Allied quadrants per the manual are 1, 2, 6, 7 (x,y < 10000), where the subtender patrols.
coordinate_system.y_axis: inferred: y grows toward the compass heading 0 (north); ORDXX1 'heading 350' and ORDXX3 'heading 225' match the first-leg vectors of COURXX1/COURXX3 with y up.

formats.duplicates: Files numbered 11-20 are byte-identical copies of 1-10 for ORDXX and COURXX, so only 10 distinct scenarios exist.

COURXX.layout: 24 rows x 7 numbers + trailer row of 3 numbers; column 0 = subtender, columns 1-6 = enemy vessels. Row 1 type codes; rows 2-3 start x/y; rows 4-5 waypoint-1 x/y; row 6 waypoint-1 speed; then waypoints 2-7 as (x row, y row, speed row).
certain: column 0 is the subtender (its coordinates stay inside quadrants 1,2,6,7)
(0,0) waypoints mark unused slots / anchored ships
inferred: type codes 3..8 = subtender, freighter, tanker, troop carrier, patrol boat, destroyer: confirmed by rendering OBX3-OBX8 and comparing with the manual's ship catalog; the orders text agrees (unescorted convoys contain only 4/5/6, 'patrol craft' scenarios are mostly 7)
COURXX.waypoint_speed_semantics: decoded at Gato1.exe 0x07a03-0x07a7b: when a ship picks waypoint W as its next target it sets speed = difficulty + (speed row of waypoint W), so the speed row is the speed used while travelling TO waypoint W. (0,0) waypoints are NOT skipped: the ship simply heads for (0,0).

statement_order: FOR k = 2 TO 8: INPUT #1, type(k)                    ' row 1 (array ds:0x1daa)
FOR k = 2 TO 8: INPUT #1, x0(k): x(k) = x0(k)        ' row 2 (ds:0x1cf6, copied to ds:0x1d3e)
FOR k = 2 TO 8: INPUT #1, y0(k): y(k) = y0(k): z(k) = 0   ' row 3 (ds:0x1d1a, copied to ds:0x1d62; ds:0x1cae cleared)
FOR w = 1 TO 7: FOR j = 1 TO 3: FOR k = 2 TO 8: INPUT #1, a(j, w, k)   ' rows 4-24, array ds:0x179e, index ((j*9 + w)*9 + k); j = 1 x, 2 y, 3 speed (loop limits 3 and 7 are inferred from the 21 rows)
INPUT #1, V1, V2, V3                                  ' trailer row: stored in ds:0x2246, 0x2242, 0x226a (assumed in file order)
verified: file columns map to ship slots 2..8 (slot 1, the player's own boat, is not read from the file)
rows 1-3 = type, start x, start y; start position is copied into a working position array
waypoint rows are stored waypoint-major: for each of 7 waypoints three rows x, y, speed
the speed row is stored together with (after) its waypoint, as parse_course assumes
every number is read with INPUT # (decimal text -> 4-byte single in memory)
not_determined: whether the objective-quadrant test also requires a minimum depth (it does not test depth)

unknown: whether the objective quadrant must also be entered 'stopped' at any depth (the code tests speed, quadrant, time of day and island distance only; it does not test depth)

trailer_decoded.objective_quadrant: trailer[0], ds:0x2246: island quadrant to reach (0 = none). Gato1.exe 0x06fef: the mission completes when the boat's speed is 0, its quadrant equals this value, TIME OF DAY equals trailer[1] and the island of that quadrant is closer than inner radius + 200.
trailer_decoded.flag_b: trailer[1], ds:0x2242: required TIME OF DAY for that island objective (1 = day, 0 = night; compared with the GAME CONTROL [3] setting, ds:0x21ca). 0 in scenarios 6-10 (e.g. ORDXX7 'SUGGEST NIGHT RESCUE').
trailer_decoded.value_c: trailer[2], ds:0x226a: highest ship slot of the convoy. The mission also completes when every ship in slots 3..value_c is sunk (slot = file column + 2; values above 8 mean all of slots 3..8). Gato1.exe 0x07bf8-0x07d9f.

formats.ORDXX: Order text; '@' prefix on line 1 is a marker before the classification. The game adds the date-time group when displaying.

inferred: radius_inner < radius_outer; the outer value (500/1000/1500) is probably the shoal or island size, the inner one the island/collision core
decoded: radius_inner (col 3, ds:0x222a) is the island collision core and objective radius; radius_outer (col 4, ds:0x222e) the second ellipse axis; attr_5 (col 5, ds:0x2382) = island picture 1..3 (one of the three DRAW strings); attr_6 (col 6, ds:0x2386) = DRAW scale S= of that picture. Gato1.exe 0x0c6c8-0x0c7d2, 0x0c9b2, 0x067db.

formats.OBX: DRAW macro language of GW-BASIC/BASICA, 16 lines per file. OBX1 = island silhouettes, OBX3-8 = ships by type code. Lines are 16 view angles (inferred from the symmetric width profile and renders). Colour command is always C0.
